currentSnapshot.note: Current fields reflect the independent full-corpus ngspice-47 review run on c53845d2 (outcome SHA256 26d5148ef8cf15ff6d8d2c2356d02cd995ca1401860c99c2e88ae274d350e2ca), reconciled for PR #1657. reportCommit identifies the measured baseline. mos-test and switches-manual-p92 now match; no root cause is inferred here. adder-bip leaves the deferred mismatch list because it exceeds the 120 s bound, not because parity improved. Historical evidence, deferred reason and measuredOn below retain original diagnostic provenance. Stochastic current values are samples, not reproducible parity claims.

measuredOn.metric: corpus-f published metric (lib.ts normalizedSignalErrors, MATCH_THRESHOLD 0.01) with the #593 per-quantity peak floor (1e-4 V for v(...), 1e-10 A for i(...), 1e-12 otherwise)
measuredOn.tool: pnpm exec tsx benchmarks/corpus/corpus-f/triage-detail.ts <fixture-id> [--tmax s] [--deck variant] [--reference-tmax s [--candidate ngspice]]
measuredOn.diagnosticLimitations: Fine-step runs do not establish step convergence. Reference-TMAX comparisons use each candidate's own grid and breakpoint alignment, so their maxima do not rank engine accuracy on a common grid.

rootCauses.summary: Control-plot export exposes a pwm-sin transient mismatch. Both engines execute; numerical parity is not established. Root cause of the measured error remains unclassified, not attributed to the harness fix.

PR #1701 adds bounded BJT DC sensitivity execution, not ngspice-47 numerical parity. The three unchanged diffpair decks now execute but mismatch on common sensitivity vectors; full parameter enumeration is also deferred.
#1572 refresh: mos-test.cir regressed from matched to unsupported saved device vector @mn1[id]; ngspice-47 still succeeds.
MOS1 treated CBD/CBS as constant capacitors and ignored CJ/CJSW/MJ/MJSW/PB/FC. Fixed by #601 (depletion junction charge); mosmem now matches.

MOS1 had no Meyer intrinsic gate capacitance from TOX. Fixed by #601 (Meyer gate charges). The remaining ltra2_2_line i(vs) gap was investigated under #627 (#629): it is step/grid discretisation, routed to #592.

BSIM3 (level 8, version 3.3.0, default parameters) 4-bit NAND adder. Before #624, supply and source currents were 10-40x ngspice-47. Between #624 and #648 it exceeded the 120 s bound. Since #648 it completes again with internal NAND nodes up to 1.54 off. Not root-caused; tracked in #626.

The transient metric interpolates ngspice's coarse default-step output onto spice-ts points, so ngspice's own truncation and interpolation error is scored as a spice-ts mismatch. On main 3b9c836f (after #689 CKTtrunc step control; not bisected) rtlinv, mos-test, fourbitadder and ltra2_2_line match; rca3040 (0.0118) and switches-manual-p92 (0.74) remain mismatches.

Signals with zero or ~100 uV ngspice peaks were normalised by that peak (floor 1e-12), so fV-uV residuals exceeded 1%. Fixed by #593: the normalising peak is floored per quantity at VNTOL/0.01 = 1e-4 V for node voltages and ABSTOL/0.01 = 1e-10 A for branch currents, uniformly for every fixture. rca3040 AC v(2) drops from 0.0564 to 5.64e-10; fourbitadder keeps 3-7 uV residuals above VNTOL (split to #698).

BSIM1/BSIM2 (LEVEL 4/5) were not implemented. The issue-table mismatch came from silently running Level-1 equations; from #552 they raised UnsupportedModelLevelError. Fixed on main by #667 (ngspice-47 BSIM1/BSIM2, LEVEL=4/5): both unchanged decks now match.
The .model VDMOS card was silently dropped. #542 made unsupported model types a typed error and #562 (#506) added the ngspice-47 VDMOS model; both VDMOS decks now match.
TRNOISE/TRRANDOM decks compare two independent random realisations: ngspice-47 reseeds every run, while spice-ts is deterministic. The sample-wise max error is meaningless and not reproducible.

fourbitadder TTL NAND internal nodes x*.8 (75-125 uV peaks) kept 1-7 uV residuals above the 1 uV VNTOL floor on b1a1ff58. Fixed by transient step control, bisected with triage-detail.ts; the BJT load, gmin and the convergence test were not involved. #689 (ngspice CKTtrunc) cut the default-step worst on the 8 sub-mV signals from 7.39 uV to 0.327 uV and the TMAX 10 ps worst over all 270 signals from 11.7 uV to 4.14 uV; #758 (ngspice dctran first step and order control) cut them to 0.148 uV and 50 nV. Guarded by the live #698 tests in triage-511.test.ts.

spice-ts-loss (unsupported S card) at bf2e4169; runnable since #579. Ideal S/W switches make v(10), v(20), v(30), v(40) jump between consecutive output points. ngspice-47's default output on the unchanged deck has 2 us between the points that bracket every edge, and spice-ts places each edge inside that interval: v(10) crosses 0.5 V at 1.20029/3.20006 ms (spice-ts) and at 1.19856-1.20056/3.19900-3.20100 ms (ngspice). Interpolating that 2 us chord gives 0.865 (abs 0.865 V, spice-ts 1 vs ngspice 0.135 at t=1.2 ms). At ngspice points: 2.7e-20. With both engines at TMAX 0.1 us, crossing times agree within 1e-8 s, but the metric still reports 1.0 because the edge is vertical. Its max over a step edge is set by sub-step timing, not by the waveform. 8/13 signals agree to <= 5.4e-16. Recorded under #592 (metric); not counted as a match. On main 3b9c836f (merge of #593 with main after #689 ngspice CKTtrunc step control, #686, #691, #696, #479; not bisected): still a mismatch, 0.74 tran v(10) (#592).
